correctness.rationale: For \(q=2^s\), \(x^2=M^{\mathsf T}x^{[2]}\), and the idempotents form the \(\mathbb F_2\)-fixed space of an invertible Frobenius-semilinear map. The minimal-dependence/Frobenius argument proves any \(\mathbb F_2\)-independent fixed k-tuple is \(\mathbb F_q\)-independent. A uniform \(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb \(\mathbb F_q\))\) matrix maps any prescribed squared q-frame to that frame with probability inverse to the total q-frame count. Hence every k-frame moment equals one, identical to the ordinary \(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb \(\mathbb F_2\))\) fixed-space moments. These moments form an invertible triangular system, establishing the full distribution. Gaussian-binomial inversion gives the displayed probabilities; the Euler product gives the n-to-infinity limit, uniformly in all \(q=2^s\). Independently executed finite-field enumeration checked six exact cases: (n,q)=(2,2),(2,4),(2,8),(3,2),(3,4),(4,2), a total of 205482 matrices. Finite checks are not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The asserted new result is the all-dimensional algebra-to-\(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb \(\mathbb F_2\))\) distributional identification, not the established finite-general-linear-group fixed-space formula. Kaygorodov–Martín González–Viruel 2026 gives the mean and a motivating random-algebra question but not this characteristic-two exact distribution. Fulman–Stanton 2015 explicitly supplies the \(\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb \(\mathbb F_2\))\) fixed-space law and is credited for that prior part. Dempwolff–Fisher–Herman 2000 treats semilinear normal forms and algebraic-closure fixed points, not a uniform finite-field idempotent law. Wei–Zou 2023 counts isomorphism classes, a different sampling statistic. Dimension-two and first-two-moment specializations can be covered by earlier enumeration but do not imply all higher-dimensional masses. An uncatalogued equivalent application remains possible; priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: The older paper Dempwolff (1990), Normal forms and fixed subspaces of semilinear maps, was not obtained in full and might contain an equivalent probability-law implication.
Wei–Zou (2023) was only compared at abstract level, though its reported invariant is different.
Exhaustive historical priority across all semilinear finite-field and random linearized-polynomial literature is not independently certified.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural exact statistical refinement of the random evolution-algebra idempotent problem. It determines the complete distribution, exact support, extension-field independence and limiting idempotent-free density in every dimension. The field-size universality is structural and is not implied by prior mean, variance or dimension-two classifications. It connects a nonlinear-algebra idempotency question with the well-developed fixed-space law for a classical finite matrix group and facilitates further probabilistic analysis. Scope is well motivated by the 2026 survey, rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
